item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"Scholz’s program was mostly explicit but diffuse. Dated statements and the National Security Strategy identified security and Ukraine support, NATO defense, energy and supply-chain resilience, modernization, climate neutrality, social cohesion, structured migration, and a more capable Europe (BATCH-0015-E001; BATCH-0014-E007; BATCH-0016-E020; BATCH-0026-E001; BATCH-0031-E006). Several goals were testable through dated targets, including 2% defense spending, 80% renewable electricity by 2030, hydrogen and grid expansion, and 15 million electric vehicles (BATCH-0005-E009; BATCH-0029-E003; BATCH-0012-E019). The program was not a single stable hierarchy: coalition conflict delayed budget decisions and obscured direction (BATCH-0013-E007; BATCH-0024-E006), the China strategy lacked binding targets and concrete dependency-reduction measures (BATCH-0007-E009), and key heating-law choices remained under negotiation (BATCH-0013-E001). The 2% defense commitment was qualified as a multi-year average rather than necessarily a 2023 result (BATCH-0015-E006). These sources establish stated and formally adopted goals, not their execution. Attribution is chiefly governmental and coalition-level, not solely personal to Scholz; moral approval or disapproval of the objectives is irrelevant to this competence lens.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E001","BATCH-0014-E007","BATCH-0016-E020","BATCH-0026-E001","BATCH-0005-E009","BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0012-E019","BATCH-0031-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E007","BATCH-0024-E006","BATCH-0007-E009","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0015-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not establish a private or informal priority hierarchy beyond repeated public choices.","Many goals were coalition, EU, or NATO commitments, limiting personal attribution.","Program clarity is better documented than prioritization, resource commitment, or outcome testing." ]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"The government translated substantial priorities into enacted laws, budgets, strategies, and institutions, but the evidence varies sharply between enacted machinery, proposals, future commitments, and actual execution. Enacted examples include the National Security Strategy, Bürgergeld, Wohngeld-Plus, the care reform, the Supply Chain Act, smart-meter legislation, municipal heat-planning legislation, competition-law amendments, whistleblower protection, electoral reform, and police-check documentation (BATCH-0014-E007; BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0027-E014; BATCH-0008-E009; BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0009-E010; BATCH-0007-E007; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0034-R05-E001). Other measures remained proposals or future-dated plans: skilled-immigration changes entered in stages and the supplied evidence does not establish their full enactment or results (BATCH-0006-E002); digital-administration, heat-plan, and data-strategy milestones extended beyond 2023 (BATCH-0009-E008; BATCH-0009-E011; BATCH-0028-E007). Operational specification was often incomplete: the China strategy lacked binding targets (BATCH-0007-E009), the National Security Council was not created (BATCH-0005-E012), and experts criticized missing standards, timelines, monitoring, and cost clarity in digitalization (BATCH-0009-E012). Auditors also found delayed projects, insufficient staffing, weak targeting, and insufficient defense funds despite the special fund (BATCH-0003-E009; BATCH-0003-E011; BATCH-0003-E012). Thus formal operationalization was substantial but uneven; Scholz’s personal role is generally not separable from ministers, Parliament, agencies, Länder, and inherited frameworks.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E007","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0027-E014","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0007-E007","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0034-R05-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E002","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0007-E009","BATCH-0005-E012","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0003-E009","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Enactment does not establish disbursement, enforcement, compliance, or outcomes.","The supplied record does not document Scholz’s individual drafting, appointment, allocation, or correction decisions.","Several measures had implementation deadlines after the target period." ]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The record shows real mobilization of state and partner networks, but effectiveness and completion were uneven. Germany mobilized THW personnel from ten local associations and specialized equipment for Slovenia’s floods (BATCH-0032-E008), operated a large BAMF system with 8,447 positions and quality-control functions (BATCH-0011-R01-E010), expanded screening capacity for the Afghan program (BATCH-0011-R03-E014), and delivered or committed substantial Ukrainian military assistance with allied coordination and training (BATCH-0026-E004; BATCH-0033-E006; BATCH-0016-E006). International and cross-border mobilization also included the Ukraine Recovery Conference, NATO coordination, and organized international-crime cooperation (BATCH-0023-E008; BATCH-0034-R10-E001; BATCH-0006-E017). Adverse evidence shows that inputs did not reliably become effective capacity: defense spending was initially slow and judged insufficient against inherited readiness deficiencies (BATCH-0015-E003; BATCH-0015-E005), ministry staffing delayed funding applications (BATCH-0003-E011), special-fund architecture weakened budget control (BATCH-0004-E001), and administrative and appointment oversight failed in documented cases (BATCH-0030-E007). Afghan admissions remained far below the intended rate, with only 13 of 229 selected people entering by October (BATCH-0011-R03-E013). The best-supported finding is substantial but domain-specific mobilization, not consistently effective or ruler-exclusive mobilization.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0011-R01-E010","BATCH-0011-R03-E014","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0033-E006","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0023-E008","BATCH-0034-R10-E001","BATCH-0006-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0030-E007","BATCH-0011-R03-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Positive evidence often establishes inputs, staffing, deliveries, or activity rather than effectiveness or completed milestones.","Responsibility was shared with ministers, Parliament, agencies, Länder, allies, industry, and local authorities.","No consolidated resource-to-outcome ledger covers the full program portfolio." ]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The evidence supports partial institutional personnel capacity but does not establish strong personal personnel management by Scholz. The Chancellor had formal authority to propose ministerial appointments and dismissals, while ministers managed departments independently; this establishes authority, not its exercise (BATCH-0035-E008). BAMF had 1,267 special officers for vulnerable applicants and 8,447 positions overall, with quality controls and screening functions (BATCH-0011-R03-E006; BATCH-0011-R01-E010). Yet capability was inconsistent: professional reports described cases in which trauma or torture indicators did not trigger specialist consultation, while BAMF did not record consultation or takeover rates (BATCH-0011-R03-E007); guardians and local systems were overloaded (BATCH-0011-R03-E009); asylum counselling could have as few as two full-time counsellors for 600 applicants at one centre (BATCH-0011-R03-E011); and federal auditors identified inadequate staffing and undocumented or non-publicly advertised leadership selections in affiliated administration (BATCH-0003-E011; BATCH-0030-E007). The Bundeswehr also remained below its personnel target, with about 181,000 personnel against a 2027 target of 203,000, while Scholz rejected conscription and preferred reservists (BATCH-0006-E006). There is little evidence of Scholz personally selecting, retaining, replacing, or disciplining implementers, so the conclusion is mixed institutional capability with weak personal attribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0035-E008","BATCH-0011-R03-E006","BATCH-0011-R01-E010","BATCH-0006-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R03-E007","BATCH-0011-R03-E009","BATCH-0011-R03-E011","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0030-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No systematic record of Scholz’s appointments, dismissals, retention decisions, or performance reviews is supplied.","Institutional staffing does not prove effective empowerment or competent selection.","The evidence is concentrated in asylum, defense, and administrative personnel rather than the full government." ]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination was demonstrable in selected domains but inconsistent across ministries, territories, and agencies. The National Security Strategy explicitly sought cross-government coordination of federal, state, and municipal crisis capacities (BATCH-0014-E007; BATCH-0012-E009), and Ukraine support involved allied coordination, training, logistics, and staged deliveries (BATCH-0016-E005; BATCH-0016-E008). Flood assistance also required coordinated mobilization across THW and local associations (BATCH-0032-E008). However, territorial and administrative follow-through was weak. Only 105 of 575 online services had met the earlier target, and experts found the corrective proposal lacking standards, timelines, cost clarity, monitoring, and a common technical model (BATCH-0009-E012); the federal government separately claimed 97 of 115 federal services were digital while most Länder and municipal services remained unavailable nationwide (BATCH-0029-E001). Auditors found delayed projects, hesitant implementation of parliamentary decisions, insufficiently targeted action, and weak administrative efficiency (BATCH-0003-E009). Federal guidance on asylum vulnerability was not systematically monitored across Länder, reception standards varied, and capacity strain caused backlogs and local failures (BATCH-0011-R03-E004; BATCH-0011-R04-E014). Coalition budget conflict and the decision not to create a National Security Council further qualify coordination (BATCH-0013-E007; BATCH-0005-E012). The evidence therefore supports domain-specific coordination, not comprehensive control or milestone compliance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E007","BATCH-0012-E009","BATCH-0016-E005","BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0029-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0003-E009","BATCH-0011-R03-E004","BATCH-0011-R04-E014","BATCH-0013-E007","BATCH-0005-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No ministry-by-ministry or Länder-wide milestone and compliance ledger is supplied.","Official coordination statements do not prove completed reach or sustained compliance.","Many failures concern coalition, ministerial, local, or inherited responsibilities rather than a personal Scholz order." ]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"Legislation and directives became observable practice in several domains, but implementation was incomplete and uneven. Bürgergeld, Wohngeld-Plus, care reform, the Supply Chain Act, smart-meter rules, heat-planning law, electoral reform, competition enforcement, whistleblower protection, and temporary protection for Ukrainians entered legal or administrative practice (BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0027-E014; BATCH-0008-E009; BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0009-E010; BATCH-0034-R05-E001; BATCH-0007-E007; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0008-E004). BAföG support also produced measurable 2023 delivery, with 635,600 recipients and €3.4 billion in spending, although fully funded school pupils declined (BATCH-0020-E007). The federal housing programme launched with allocated funding, but uptake and completed homes were not shown (BATCH-0027-E003; BATCH-0027-E005). Adverse evidence is material: Afghan admissions were severely delayed (BATCH-0011-R03-E013), independent asylum counselling suffered delayed and insufficient funding (BATCH-0011-R03-E011), digitalization missed its earlier target (BATCH-0009-E012), auditors found delayed projects, weak administration, and inadequate staffing (BATCH-0003-E009; BATCH-0003-E011), and the child-basic-income project remained stalled amid coalition financing disputes (BATCH-0005-E006; BATCH-0005-E018). Energy relief, LNG, and Ukraine support show activity, but some evidence is official self-report or delivery commitments rather than independent outcome verification. Thus implementation was real but substantially incomplete, with mostly government-level rather than personal Scholz attribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0027-E014","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0034-R05-E001","BATCH-0007-E007","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0027-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0011-R03-E011","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0003-E009","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0005-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many positive items establish legal commencement, program design, or official delivery rather than nationwide uptake, quality, or outcomes.","Several deadlines and benefits extended beyond 2023.","Shared federal-state implementation and inherited programs limit personal attribution." ]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Progress toward the frozen program was mixed and only partly attributable to Scholz’s government. Energy-crisis measures plausibly prevented a deeper downturn: DIW estimated that relief and stabilization supported consumption, with transfers benefiting lower-income households more than tax relief, though the findings were model-based and mixed in distribution (BATCH-0034-R12-E001; BATCH-0034-R12-E003; BATCH-0034-R12-E004; BATCH-0034-R12-E006). Energy security improved through LNG, storage, and supplier diversification, but the strongest attribution came from Scholz’s own accounts and depended on states, firms, and external conditions (BATCH-0016-E018; BATCH-0029-E002). Against this, GDP fell 0.3%, private consumption 0.8%, construction investment 2.1%, and housing approvals 26.6%; unemployment rose, while employment reached a record level (BATCH-0028-E001; BATCH-0028-E002; BATCH-0009-E021; BATCH-0023-E001). Distributional results were uneven: child poverty risk fell to 14.0% but 23.9% of children remained at risk of poverty or social exclusion, and overall poverty risk was 14.4% (BATCH-0024-E001; BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0019-E001). BAföG recipients and spending rose, social-assistance and care spending rose, and effective wages—especially at the bottom—improved, but these are not ruler-attributed causal measures (BATCH-0020-E006; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0035-E007). Defense readiness remained below inherited needs and Afghan implementation lagged, while family-reunification visas met the annual quota (BATCH-0015-E003; BATCH-0015-E005; BATCH-0011-R06-E006). External shocks, ECB policy, inherited weaknesses, coalition constraints, and realistic lags prevent a clear net advance across the full portfolio.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0034-R12-E001","BATCH-0034-R12-E003","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0034-R12-E006","BATCH-0016-E018","BATCH-0028-E002","BATCH-0009-E021","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0035-E007","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0011-R06-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E001","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0023-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many outcomes have lag, preliminary status, income-reference limitations, or model assumptions.","No complete counterfactual separates Scholz’s contribution from war, energy prices, ECB policy, private decisions, allies, or inherited capacity.","Longer-term climate, modernization, and defense outcomes were not yet observable by end-2023." ]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"The evidence supports some specific adaptation, but not systematic learning or consistent implementer replacement. The Afghan program was paused after alleged misuse concerns, additional checks and security interviews were introduced, screening capacity expanded, and the program restarted; however, the government reported no systemic abuse and admissions remained very low, so this is a procedural adjustment with incomplete correction rather than demonstrated success (BATCH-0011-R03-E013; BATCH-0011-R03-E014; BATCH-0011-R01-E004). BAMF also updated country-of-origin information in autumn 2023 after criticism concerning Russian military-age applicants, but the record presents competing NGO and BAMF accounts and no outcome proof (BATCH-0011-R04-E003). Other partial adaptations included police-check documentation, the repatriate-law amendment responding to court-driven administrative practice, and proposed reforms to surveillance and digital administration (BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0033-E024; BATCH-0033-E025; BATCH-0010-E009; BATCH-0027-E015). After the Constitutional Court ruling, Scholz accepted the Court’s authority and initiated or proposed supplementary-budget, spending-freeze, and reprioritization measures; the supplied evidence does not establish final enactment or effects (BATCH-0016-E016; BATCH-0016-E017). Audits nevertheless documented delayed projects, insufficient staffing, underused military schools, weak targeting, and ineffective administration without supplied proof of completed follow-up (BATCH-0002-E002; BATCH-0003-E009; BATCH-0003-E013; BATCH-0003-E015). Digitalization missed targets, and BAMF specialist controls did not demonstrate corrected referral failures (BATCH-0009-E012; BATCH-0011-R03-E007). Scholz acknowledged low child-supplement uptake and the need to increase it, but no successful correction is shown (BATCH-0016-E011). Overall, adaptation was selective and reactive, with limited evidence of learning from audits or replacing failed implementers.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0011-R03-E014","BATCH-0011-R01-E004","BATCH-0011-R04-E003","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0033-E024","BATCH-0033-E025","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0016-E016","BATCH-0016-E017","BATCH-0016-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0003-E009","BATCH-0003-E013","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0011-R03-E007","BATCH-0011-R06-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Audits identify failures more often than they document completed recommendations or improved outcomes.","The budget response was partly compelled by judicial intervention and remained partly proposed at the supplied cutoff.","No systematic record of dismissals, replacements, or Chancellor-level performance management is supplied." ]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"Scholz’s crisis management preserved some objectives through formal decisions and organized responses, but outcomes and durability were mixed. In Ukraine, the government supplied weapons, training, logistics, and air defense while coordinating with allies and seeking to avoid NATO-Russia escalation; the Leopard decision was initially delayed and the record does not establish that escalation was prevented or military objectives achieved (BATCH-0016-E002; BATCH-0016-E005; BATCH-0026-E004; BATCH-0031-E001; BATCH-0029-E010). In the Israel-Hamas crisis, Scholz pursued regional contacts, hostage release, humanitarian access, and de-escalation, while reviewing Palestinian cooperation and pausing new funding; the evidence does not establish that his efforts caused hostage releases or protected civilians, and Germany’s military support for Israel and limited public condemnation of alleged violations create a material qualification (BATCH-0029-E007; BATCH-0029-E008; BATCH-0031-E002; BATCH-0033-E011; BATCH-0008-E016; BATCH-0011-R04-E005). He also supported mediation and constitutional restoration during the Niger coup and directed rapid flood assistance to Slovenia, showing responses beyond the principal wars (BATCH-0032-E008; BATCH-0032-E009). Migration crises produced expanded border controls, asylum reforms, and additional federal-state funding, but reception capacity, backlogs, counselling access, and failed removals remained serious problems (BATCH-0011-R01-E003; BATCH-0011-R04-E014; BATCH-0011-R05-E005; BATCH-0011-R04-E013). Domestically, energy measures maintained supply and moderated economic disruption, while the Constitutional Court budget ruling forced acceptance of legal constraints and proposed corrective measures; final implementation is not established (BATCH-0034-R12-E001; BATCH-0016-E016; BATCH-0024-E013). Thus crisis responses were active and sometimes coordinated, but delays, legal failure, capacity strain, and unverified outcomes prevent a consistently effective conclusion. Subnational protest policing is not personally attributable to Scholz on the supplied evidence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E005","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0029-E008","BATCH-0031-E002","BATCH-0033-E011","BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0032-E009","BATCH-0011-R01-E003","BATCH-0011-R04-E013","BATCH-0034-R12-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0029-E010","BATCH-0008-E016","BATCH-0011-R04-E005","BATCH-0011-R04-E014","BATCH-0011-R05-E005","BATCH-0016-E016","BATCH-0024-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence records decisions and diplomatic activity more clearly than crisis outcomes.","Hostage, de-escalation, civilian-protection, energy, and Ukrainian-support effects are not independently established.","The budget response includes proposed measures whose final enactment and effects are not supplied.","Federal, Länder, municipal, EU, NATO, and external actors materially constrain attribution." ]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By year-end, Scholz’s government had converted more of its program into formal law, strategies, and operating arrangements than was visible at the start of the period, but the evidence does not show durable achievement across the full portfolio. A bounded start/end comparison is: security and Ukraine—program announced in 2022 and formalized through the 2023 National Security Strategy, defense fund, procurement, deployments, and continuing aid, but readiness and funding adequacy remained disputed (BATCH-0015-E001; BATCH-0014-E007; BATCH-0016-E006; BATCH-0015-E003; BATCH-0015-E005); energy—rapid LNG, storage, and supply diversification became observable practice, while long-term climate and industrial financing was disrupted by the court ruling (BATCH-0016-E018; BATCH-0024-E013); social policy—Bürgergeld, Wohngeld-Plus, care reform, BAföG delivery, and housing-support programs operated, but child poverty, care pressures, and service gaps persisted (BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0027-E014; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0024-E001; BATCH-0022-E009); modernization—smart-meter, heat-planning, supply-chain, competition, whistleblower, and electoral reforms were enacted, but digitalization missed targets and many milestones were future-dated (BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0009-E010; BATCH-0008-E009; BATCH-0007-E007; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0034-R05-E001; BATCH-0009-E012); migration—temporary protection and some family-reunification delivery were achieved, while Afghan admissions, reception capacity, counselling, and removals remained fragile (BATCH-0008-E004; BATCH-0011-R06-E006; BATCH-0011-R03-E013; BATCH-0011-R04-E014; BATCH-0011-R03-E011; BATCH-0011-R05-E005). Economic outcomes were weak or mixed: GDP, consumption, construction, and housing approvals fell, while employment and some lower-income wage measures improved (BATCH-0028-E001; BATCH-0028-E002; BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0035-E007). The defensible conclusion is partial conversion with fragile durability, not demonstrated durable realization of a greater share of the whole program. Personal attribution is limited by coalition government, Parliament, Länder, agencies, allies, inherited conditions, shocks, and judicial constraints; moral effects did not affect this execution assessment.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E001","BATCH-0014-E007","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0016-E018","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0027-E014","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0007-E007","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0034-R05-E001","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0011-R06-E006","BATCH-0028-E002","BATCH-0035-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0024-E013","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0022-E009","BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0011-R04-E014","BATCH-0011-R03-E011","BATCH-0011-R05-E005","BATCH-0028-E001","BATCH-0023-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The start/end comparison is bounded and qualitative because no complete frozen-program ledger is supplied.","Many end-period items are laws, plans, or future milestones rather than durable outcomes.","Post-2023 evidence would be needed to test persistence of institutions, capacity, and achieved results.","Aggregate outcomes cannot be attributed solely to Scholz." ]}],"cross_lens_observations":["The evidence consistently shows a stronger record of explicit program definition and formal legal conversion than of coordinated execution, adaptive correction, or durable outcomes.","Positive implementation evidence is strongest where concrete laws, deliveries, staffing, or administrative counts are available; official claims and future commitments are treated as weaker than independent audits and outcome series.","The central attribution constraint is collective governance: many findings concern the federal government, coalition, ministries, agencies, Länder, municipalities, Parliament, EU, or NATO rather than Scholz personally.","Moral evaluation is separate from effectiveness throughout: the assessment concerns whether stated or reliably revealed objectives were converted into action and results, regardless of their desirability."]}
